expects.description: One of the project's governance and communication documents is on file in the compliance documents and was refreshed within the last year. Either document satisfies the clause. The list of accepted documents differs on purpose from the one for the information-security policy clause in ISO 27001.
Each high-risk requirement has an implementation plan that includes its threat model.
A per-requirement risk assessment summarises the risks opened, mitigated or accepted for the change. This is the direct evidence for the clause.
Periodic reviews of control effectiveness are on file. A review older than a year still counts but is shown as expired.
Role-based access and a second authentication factor are built into the portal, so the control is part of how the portal works.
A per-requirement security summary records the access-control review.
Operational incidents are on file as incident reports.
The pass or fail outcome of each pipeline gate is recorded.
Smoke-test results from after a production deployment show that production is being monitored.

Met by a release approval made by someone other than the release's creator or submitter. A release approved by its own creator or submitter, where the project's approval policy allows it with a recorded gap, is recorded as a self-approval instead and is shown as a gap.
Test results from the delivery pipeline show that processing behaves as specified.
Evidence is served only through signed links that expire within an hour, so the control is part of how the portal works.
